tests.proves: negative 7's named test: the persona session's recorded expiry is bound to a value asserted by the trusted server under the service-role trust boundary, read from the token it minted; no refresh material is persisted, returned or usable; no persona holds an independently usable credential; and the session cookie expires with the token. the evaluation school offers exactly five personas from the frozen role model, and no SYSTEM_ADMIN perspective exists to be offered (ADR-0020, amended)
a person who is not a live evaluator is refused by name at the hub, not shown an empty list
an institution administrator cannot acquire evaluator status by any path: table refusal, no client grant on grant_evaluator, and evaluator status is not a role
a real person's id is refused as a persona id, and an allow-list row pointing at a real person is refused by name
no persona account carries a credential, and assume_persona is reachable only by the server: no persona session can be created outside the assume flow
a persona cannot reach the assumption path at all, so a persona-to-persona transition is impossible by privilege. NEGATIVES 5 AND 6 ARE ONE CONTROL and this is recorded rather than staged as two
one effective persona at a time per evaluator: refused by name, and by a unique index under concurrency

negative 7, DATABASE HALF ONLY: the recorded expiry is the token's to the instant and a dead token opens nothing. The enforcement is the token itself and is pinned by EVAL-S01 -- this suite authenticates with set_config and bypasses JWT verification by construction, so nothing here can distinguish a live token from a dead one. ARGUED, NOT TESTED, in this layer
the assumed DEAN is refused exactly what a DEAN is refused (INV-19) while remaining a member of its own school: the boundary is exercised, not bypassed
no persona credential exists to leak: no password on any persona account, no credential-shaped text in any audit or session row
an unapproved official_evidence_purpose cannot be spelled, a second institution cannot occupy an approved one, and all three evaluation tables refuse production by trigger
an action taken as a persona carries both identities, and the trail-wide dual-identity property holds
exit ends the pairing server-side, the indicator disappears because it reads the session, and the exit event itself carries both identities

the evaluation school's evidence is OFFICIAL through the ordinary cap model -- the same expression that proves it for D1 -- and derive_evidence_class reads neither the flag, nor tenant_kind, nor the purpose
no authorization root and no RLS policy knows the evaluation facility exists (ADR-0020 §3.1)

certificate issuance on the demonstration journey, end to end: the learner persona's genuine OFFICIAL, ELIGIBLE session reaches a sealed certificate through the ordinary server-held CERT_SECRET_KEY_V1 and verifies through the one public route, still returning exactly the five D3b fields and naming nothing about the evaluation facility. Also pins that the issuance route checks session_is_mine with the CALLER's own client BEFORE the service client is reached -- ordering, not presence -- and that no seed file reaches for a signing secret

baseline integrity by content, not by marker: every document listed in docs/rebuild/BASELINE-MANIFEST.json is byte-identical to the frozen baseline, every file in a governed directory is listed by the manifest, each document's own amendment marker agrees with its manifest entry, and no ungoverned second copy of a governed document exists anywhere in the repository. Retires DOC-S01, which counted markers — doc 03 carried the right marker while still stale, and three of eighteen documents carry none

ADR-0021: every function created in a migration authored since the ADR is revoked from EXECUTE on PUBLIC in that same migration, by name or by a family pattern whose resulting count is asserted. EXECUTE is granted to PUBLIC by default and `alter default privileges` cannot revoke it, so 49 migrations have carried the revoke by convention and it has been forgotten twice. The check is order-aware (a revoke before the create closes nothing) and exempts a function dropped in the same migration, which never commits

sanitized_item executes to a successful return and the projection contains the stem and options only: the item's real option rationale appears nowhere in the output, no correctness-shaped key is present, no option carries its own label, and every key is inside the declared safe set. Found by the happy-path sweep, which showed this function had never run successfully under any migration, seed or test. Asserts absence of the real secret, not presence of a return

a presented item belonging to another person and a uuid that does not exist produce the identical refusal from sanitized_item, so existence is not an oracle. The previous body raised 'unknown presented item' before authorizing — the same check-then-authorize inversion 0073 removed from metric_evaluate

every item_type_registry.sanitizer_allowlist is inside the declared safe set {item_type, stem, stimulus, opsi}, enforced by a CHECK rather than by convention, so widening the learner projection requires a migration; no projection is empty; and sanitized_item and session_paper both authorize before disclosing anything, existence included

Question Health over REAL OFFICIAL evidence: 160 learners in the D1 bootstrap tenant drive one item to correctness 1.0 and another to 0.0; both reach SIGNAL_RAISED and no other item does. Asserts the least-sampled item's actual count against the catalogue threshold, so a run whose draw under-samples says so rather than mis-measuring. The migration probes proved the mechanism; this proves the mechanism over evidence, which is where 0076's illegal birth state was found

evidence withdrawn by an integrity reviewer drives the downward pair on real data: 47 sessions reclassified out of OFFICIAL drop an item from 76 responses to 29, and it walks SIGNAL_RAISED -> OBSERVING -> INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE as two declared edges and two audit rows ordered by identity. enforce_evidence_override is INSERT-only and refuses promotion, so the OFFICIAL pool only shrinks and a state resting on withdrawn evidence is the failure these edges exist to prevent

the analytics cohort is isolated inside the one tenant that can produce OFFICIAL evidence: it has its own CLASS node and assignment, the bootstrap learner remains outside it with its own class and certificate, and the cohort issues no certificates. D1's single enrolment is the below-threshold case only if that separation holds, so it is asserted rather than assumed

the copy/route inventory (§7) IS the fetch list for the output-level INTERNAL_WORDS scan, and it is derived from src/app rather than written down: every route the application serves must appear in ROUTE_INVENTORY or this fails. F01-S03's source scan matches JSX text nodes and deliberately ignores {...} expressions, so it is structurally blind to {item.state} rendering an enum; only fetched HTML catches that, and only for routes that are fetched. A hand-maintained list would hold for the surfaces this phase adds and lapse silently for the next one

every route in the inventory is fetched unauthenticated and its rendered output scanned for internal words. Unauthenticated on purpose: a stranger's view is the widest audience any page has, so an enum reaching it has reached the worst reader. Scales automatically as routes are added, because F06-S02 fails if a served route is absent from the list

no src/app surface interpolates an enum-bearing value into a JSX TEXT POSITION. The enum-bearing column names are derived from every `create type ... as enum` in the migrations and the columns declared with them, so a new enum column is covered the day it is created. Complements both existing scans and catches what each was built to miss: F01-S03 skips {...} expressions by design, and F06-R01's unauthenticated fetch cannot reach a Studio route. Found five live leaks on first run -- bank_type, three renderings of mode, and integrity category -- none of which is an INTERNAL_WORD, so no word list would have caught them
